examples.en: The lawmaker was expelled from the party.
I'm really upset that the club decided to expel me.

examples.ko: 규칙을 어기면 제명 처분을 받을 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you break the rules, you can be expelled.
The members were shocked by the news of the expulsion.
The association canceled the player's expulsion.
Whether to expel him will be decided at the next meeting.

explain: 정당, 협회, 동아리처럼 단체가 구성원의 자격을 없애고 내보낼 때 써요. 스스로 나가는 '탈퇴'와 달리 단체가 결정해서 내보내는 거예요. 뉴스에서는 '제명 처분'이라는 말로 나와요.
explain_en: It is used when a group such as a party, an association or a club removes someone's membership and sends them out. Unlike '탈퇴' (leaving by yourself), the group makes the decision. In the news it appears as '제명 처분' (expulsion measure).

examples.en: The school club decided to expel a member.
The party expelled that lawmaker.

examples.ko: 단체가 규칙을 어긴 사람을 제명할 수 있어요.
examples.en: An organization can expel someone who broke the rules.
The members proposed expelling the president by vote.
Why are you trying to expel me from the group?

examples.ko: 협회는 부정을 저지른 선수를 제명하지 않았어요.
examples.en: The association did not expel the player who cheated.

explain: 'N을/를 제명하다'처럼 단체가 사람을 명단에서 빼 내보낼 때 써요. 일상에서 친구끼리는 '쫓아내다'라고 가볍게 말하기도 하지만, 제명하다는 공식적인 결정이라는 느낌이에요. 반대로 받아 주는 건 '가입시키다'예요.
explain_en: Used as 'N을/를 제명하다' when a group removes a person from its list and sends them out. Friends might casually say '쫓아내다', but 제명하다 sounds like an official decision. The opposite is letting someone in, '가입시키다'.

examples.ko: 내년 예산 책정은 아직 끝나지 않았어요.
examples.en: Setting next year's budget isn't finished yet.
What are the standards for setting the price?

examples.ko: 이번 행사는 예산 책정부터 다시 해야 해요.
examples.en: For this event, we have to redo the budget setting from the start.

examples.ko: 임금 책정이 공정하지 않다는 불만이 많아요.
examples.en: There are many complaints that wage setting isn't fair.

examples.ko: 회사가 가격 책정에 실수를 해서 손해를 봤어요.
examples.en: The company made a mistake in pricing and took a loss.
Please explain how the insurance fee is set.

explain: 가격, 예산, 임금처럼 숫자로 된 것을 공식적으로 정할 때 써요. 일상에서는 그냥 '정하다'라고 하고, '가격 책정, 예산 책정'처럼 짝으로 많이 써요.
explain_en: It is used when officially deciding figures such as prices, budgets and wages. In daily talk people simply say '정하다', and 책정 mostly comes in pairs like '가격 책정' and '예산 책정'.

examples.en: A lot of budget was set aside for scholarships this year.

examples.ko: 입장료가 너무 비싸게 책정된 것 같아요.
examples.en: I think the admission fee was set too high.
How is the price of this product set?

examples.ko: 임금은 경력에 따라 책정되는 경우가 많아요.
examples.en: Wages are often set according to experience.

examples.ko: 새 버스 요금은 아직 책정되지 않았어요.
examples.en: The new bus fare hasn't been set yet.

examples.ko: 행사 예산이 어디에 책정돼 있는지 알아요?
examples.en: Do you know where the event budget has been allocated?

explain: 주어는 보통 가격, 예산, 임금 같은 것이에요. 일상에서는 '정해지다'를 더 많이 쓰고, 사람이 정하는 쪽으로 말할 때는 '책정하다'를 써요.
explain_en: The subject is usually a price, budget or wage. In daily talk '정해지다' is more common, and when you focus on the person who sets it, you use '책정하다'.

examples.en: He received great praise from the people.

examples.ko: 그 의사 선생님은 마을 사람들의 칭송이 자자해요.
examples.en: People in the town are full of praise for that doctor.
I heard more criticism than praise.

examples.ko: 그 소방관의 용기는 칭송의 대상이 됐어요.
examples.en: That firefighter's courage became an object of praise.
My mother was happy about the praise for the children.

examples.ko: 모두의 칭송 속에 선수가 경기장을 떠났어요.
examples.en: The player left the stadium amid everyone's praise.

explain: '칭찬'보다 격식 있고, 사람의 업적이나 덕을 크게 기릴 때 어울려요. 보통 '칭송을 받다'로 쓰고, 친구에게 하는 가벼운 칭찬에는 쓰지 않아요. 반대말은 '비난'이에요.
explain_en: It is more formal than '칭찬' and fits when someone's achievements or virtue are highly honored. It is usually used as '칭송을 받다' and not for light compliments to a friend. The opposite is '비난' (blame).

examples.en: People praised that doctor's sacrifice.

examples.ko: 역사책은 그 왕을 훌륭한 지도자로 칭송해요.
examples.en: History books praise that king as a great leader.
Fans are praising the player's effort.
His courage deserves everyone's praise.

examples.ko: 그의 선행을 칭송하는 글이 신문에 실렸어요.
examples.en: An article praising his good deeds ran in the newspaper.
Nobody praised that work.

explain: '칭찬하다'보다 격식 있고 무게가 있어서 업적이나 덕 같은 큰 것에 어울려요. 일상 대화에서 친구나 가족을 칭찬할 때는 '칭찬하다'를 쓰는 게 자연스러워요.
explain_en: It is more formal and weighty than '칭찬하다', fitting big things like achievements or virtue. When praising a friend or family member in daily talk, '칭찬하다' sounds more natural.

examples.en: He earned the title 'the nation's singer'.
You should use the correct title for your teacher.
The title 'hero of the World Cup' was attached to that player.
This title isn't given to just anyone.
Is it okay to call him by name only, without a title?
They give the champion title to the winner of the contest.

explain: '사장님', '박사'처럼 이름 앞뒤에 붙이는 말이나, 업적 때문에 붙은 이름(국민 가수)을 가리켜요. '호칭'은 사람을 부르는 말에 초점이 있고, 칭호는 지위나 명예를 나타내는 이름에 많이 써요. '칭호를 얻다/받다/붙다'로 써요.
explain_en: It refers to a name attached to a person such as '사장님' or '박사', or a name earned through achievements, like '국민 가수'. '호칭' focuses on the word you use to address someone, while 칭호 is often used for a name showing rank or honor. It goes with '칭호를 얻다/받다/붙다'.

examples.en: Bananas are high in potassium.
Potassium helps regulate salt in the body.

examples.ko: 신장이 안 좋으면 칼륨 섭취를 조심해야 해요.
examples.en: If your kidneys are weak, you have to be careful about potassium intake.

examples.ko: 칼륨 부족은 피로의 원인이 될 수 있어요.
examples.en: A lack of potassium can cause tiredness.

examples.ko: 땀을 많이 흘리면 칼륨도 함께 빠져나가요.
examples.en: When you sweat a lot, potassium also leaves the body.
I checked the potassium content on the supplement label.

explain: 영양 성분표나 건강 정보에서 '나트륨'과 함께 자주 보이는 말이에요. 영어 potassium을 읽은 '포타슘'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: You often see it next to '나트륨' (sodium) on nutrition labels and in health information. It is also called '포타슘', from the English word potassium.

examples.en: We have to break down old prejudices.
That movie broke down gender stereotypes.
You need courage to break a bad practice.
The government promised to root out corruption.

examples.ko: 신입 사원이 낡은 문화를 타파하는 데 앞장섰어요.
examples.en: The new employee took the lead in breaking down the outdated culture.
A slogan calling to end discrimination rang out in the square.

explain: '깨다'나 '부수다'와 달리 편견, 관행, 제도, 고정관념처럼 눈에 안 보이는 것에 써요. '악습 타파', '고정관념 타파'처럼 연설이나 기사에서 자주 보이는 짝이 있어요. 일상 대화에서는 '깨다'가 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: Unlike '깨다' or '부수다', it is used for invisible things such as prejudice, customs, systems and stereotypes. It has pairings like '악습 타파' and '고정관념 타파' seen in speeches and articles. In everyday talk, '깨다' sounds more natural.

examples.en: The soldiers made a long march from dawn.
I got blisters on my feet during the march.

examples.ko: 신병 훈련에서 가장 힘든 건 행군이에요.
examples.en: The hardest part of recruit training is the march.

examples.ko: 야간 행군은 길이 어두워서 더 힘들어요.
examples.en: Night marches are harder because the road is dark.

examples.ko: 행군이 끝나자 다들 그 자리에 주저앉았어요.
examples.en: When the march ended, everyone sank down on the spot.

examples.ko: 이틀 동안 이어진 행군 끝에 목적지에 도착했어요.
examples.en: After a march that lasted two days, we reached the destination.

explain: 군인이 대열을 지어 먼 길을 걷는 훈련이나 이동을 말해요. 축제나 시위에서 줄지어 나아가는 건 '행진'이라고 해서 서로 달라요. '행군을 하다'로 많이 써요.
explain_en: It means soldiers walking a long distance in formation, as training or movement. Walking in lines at a festival or protest is '행진', which is different. It is often used as '행군을 하다'.

examples.en: The soldiers marched along the snowy road.
How many kilometers do you march per day?

examples.ko: 우리는 비가 오는데도 계속 행군해야 했어요.
examples.en: We had to keep marching even though it was raining.
The unit decided to march to the top of the mountain.
The soldiers are marching in line.
Everyone is exhausted from marching all night.

explain: 주로 군대가 훈련이나 이동을 위해 오래 걸을 때 써요. 퍼레이드나 시위처럼 줄지어 걷는 건 '행진하다'를 쓰는 게 자연스러워요.
explain_en: It is mainly used when an army walks a long way for training or movement. For parades or protests, '행진하다' is the more natural verb.

examples.en: Um, where did you put that, you know, book?
I met what's-his-name yesterday. What was his name again?

examples.ko: 거시기가 뭔지 알죠? 그거 좀 가져다주세요.
examples.en: You know that thing, right? Please bring it over.
Oh, you know, that person.
It's a bit of an awkward topic, so it's hard to say.
When my grandmother gets stuck for words, she says 'geosigi'.

explain: 이름이 갑자기 기억나지 않거나 바로 말하기 곤란할 때 사람, 물건, 일을 대신 가리키는 말이에요. 말투가 편하고 구어체라서 발표나 면접 같은 격식 있는 자리에서는 쓰지 않아요. '그거', '그 뭐더라'와 비슷하게 쓰여요.
explain_en: It stands in for a person, thing or matter when you suddenly can't recall the name or find it awkward to say directly. It is casual and spoken, so avoid it in formal settings like presentations or interviews. It works much like '그거' or '그 뭐더라'.

examples.ko: 어머니가 주신 편지를 고이 간직하고 있어요.
examples.en: I keep the letter my mother gave me safe and treasured.
I folded the clothes neatly and put them in the drawer.
The baby fell peacefully asleep.
My parents raised me with great care.
I wrapped the gift carefully and gave it to my friend.
My grandfather keeps the old photos safe and sound.

explain: '곱게, 소중하게, 조용히'라는 느낌으로 '간직하다, 접다, 잠들다, 기르다' 같은 동사와 잘 어울려요. 물이 고인다는 동사 '고이다'와는 전혀 다른 말이에요. 말투가 조금 정감 있고 글에 어울려요.
explain_en: It carries a feel of 'gently, preciously, quietly' and pairs well with verbs like '간직하다', '접다', '잠들다' and '기르다'. It is a completely different word from the verb '고이다' (water collecting). It sounds a little warm and suits writing.

examples.en: That player is the biggest contributor to the victory.

examples.ko: 건국 공신들은 나라에서 큰 상을 받았어요.
examples.en: The founding heroes received great rewards from the country.

examples.ko: 이번 프로젝트 성공의 공신은 바로 우리 팀장님이에요.
examples.en: The one who made this project a success is our team leader.

examples.ko: 그를 승리의 공신으로 칭찬하는 사람이 많아요.
examples.en: Many people praise him as the key to the victory.
I felt hurt because I wasn't treated like a key contributor.

examples.ko: 신입 사원이 매출 상승의 공신이 됐어요.
examples.en: The new employee became the reason sales went up.

explain: 원래는 나라에 큰 공을 세운 사람을 가리켰어요. 지금은 '일등 공신'처럼 어떤 일이 잘되게 한 사람이나 원인을 가볍게 말할 때도 많이 써요. 같은 소리의 '공신(공부의 신)'이라는 신조어와는 달라요.
explain_en: It originally referred to someone who rendered great service to the nation. Today it is also used lightly, as in '일등 공신', for a person or cause that made something succeed. It is different from the slang '공신' meaning a study genius.

examples.en: I read the club regulations and then joined.

examples.ko: 이 규약은 모든 회원이 지켜야 해요.
examples.en: All members have to follow this agreement.

examples.ko: 규약에 따라 회비를 매달 내야 해요.
examples.en: According to the rules, you have to pay the fee every month.
At the general meeting, they decided to make new regulations.
If rule violations continue, your activities get suspended.

examples.ko: 국제 규약이 바뀌어서 신청 방법도 달라졌어요.
examples.en: The international rules changed, so the application method changed too.

explain: 단체나 모임 안에서 서로 지키기로 정한 약속을 말해요. 학교나 일상의 '규칙', 나라의 '법'보다 모임이나 조직 내부의 문서화된 약속이라는 느낌이에요. 비슷한 말로 '회칙'이 있어요.
explain_en: It is the set of promises that members of a group or organization agree to follow. Compared with everyday '규칙' or national '법', it feels like a written agreement inside a group. A similar word is '회칙'.

examples.en: The kid next door is so unruly.

examples.ko: 극성스럽게 짖는 강아지 때문에 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.en: I couldn't sleep because of a puppy barking wildly.

examples.ko: 그 엄마는 아이 교육에 극성스러운 편이에요.
examples.en: That mother is rather overzealous about her child's education.
The relentless mosquitoes disappeared once autumn came.

examples.ko: 팬들이 극성스러워서 가수가 밖에 나가기 힘들대요.
examples.en: I hear the fans are so intense that the singer finds it hard to go out.
I want to raise a child who isn't too wild.

explain: 지나치게 열성적이거나 유난스러워서 주변이 부담스러울 때 쓰는 말로, 대체로 좋지 않은 뉘앙스예요. 아이 교육에 열심인 부모를 '극성 엄마'라고 부르기도 해요. ㅂ 불규칙이라 '극성스러워요, 극성스러운'으로 바뀌어요.
explain_en: It describes someone excessively eager or fussy to the point of being a burden to others, and usually has a negative tone. Parents very intense about their kids' education are sometimes called '극성 엄마'. It is a ㅂ-irregular adjective: '극성스러워요, 극성스러운'.

examples.en: The puppet danced in the puppet show.
He is just the boss's puppet.

examples.ko: 나는 누구의 꼭두각시도 되고 싶지 않아요.
examples.en: I don't want to be anyone's puppet.
I looked at traditional puppets at the museum.
Don't just do as you're told like a puppet.

examples.ko: 그 회사 대표를 꼭두각시라고 부르는 기사가 나왔어요.
examples.en: An article came out calling the company's CEO a puppet.

explain: 줄이나 막대로 움직이는 전통 인형을 말하고, 비유로 남이 시키는 대로만 움직이는 사람을 가리킬 때도 많이 써요. 비유로 쓰면 비난하는 느낌이 강해서 사람 앞에서 말할 때는 조심해야 해요. 영어의 puppet처럼 쓰는 거예요.
explain_en: It refers to a traditional puppet moved by strings or sticks, and is also widely used figuratively for a person who only does what others tell them. Used figuratively it sounds quite accusing, so be careful saying it to someone. It works like the English word 'puppet'.

examples.en: When sperm and an egg cell meet, fertilization happens.

examples.ko: 여성은 한 달에 한 번 난자를 배출해요.
examples.en: A woman releases an egg cell once a month.

examples.ko: 난자 냉동 보관에 관한 기사를 읽었어요.
examples.en: I read an article about freezing egg cells.
I heard an explanation about egg donation.

examples.ko: 생물 시간에 난자와 정자의 차이를 배웠어요.
examples.en: In biology class, I learned the difference between eggs and sperm.
A fertilized egg grows into an embryo.

explain: 생물이나 의학에서 암컷의 생식세포를 말하고, 짝이 되는 말은 '정자'예요. 음식으로 먹는 달걀과는 다르고, 소리가 같은 다른 말이 있으니 문맥으로 구분해야 해요. 일상에서는 주로 수업, 뉴스, 병원 이야기에서 나와요.
explain_en: It is the female reproductive cell in biology and medicine, and its pair is '정자' (sperm). It is not the egg you eat, which is '달걀'. Another word sounds the same, so tell them apart by context. In daily life it mostly comes up in classes, news and hospital talk.

examples.en: That driver is so reckless.
Reckless driving causes accidents.
The dog suddenly started barking wildly.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 화가 나면 말투가 난폭해져요.
examples.en: When he gets angry, his way of speaking turns rough.

examples.ko: 난폭한 장면이 많아서 아이와 보기 힘들어요.
examples.en: There are many violent scenes, so it's hard to watch with a child.
We solve problems in a way that isn't violent.

explain: 행동이나 말투, 운전이 거칠고 사나워서 남에게 해를 줄 것 같을 때 써요. '거칠다'는 물건의 표면에도 쓰지만 난폭하다는 사람이나 동물의 행동에 주로 써요. 뉴스에서 '난폭 운전'이라는 말로 자주 보여요.
explain_en: It is used when actions, speech or driving are rough and fierce enough that they might harm others. '거칠다' can also describe a surface, but 난폭하다 is mainly used for the behavior of people or animals. You often see it in the news as '난폭 운전' (reckless driving).

examples.en: The lobby floor is marble, so it's slippery.
The marble stairs sparkled in the sunlight.
This statue is made of white marble.
A marble dining table is pretty but expensive.
I spilled coffee on the marble and a stain was left.
I bought marble-pattern wallpaper and put it up.

explain: 건물 바닥, 조각, 주방 상판처럼 건축과 인테리어에서 자주 나오는 단단한 돌이에요. '대리석 무늬'처럼 진짜 돌이 아니어도 무늬를 말할 때 써요. 비슷한 돌로 '화강암'이 있어요.
explain_en: It is a hard stone that often appears in architecture and interiors, such as floors, sculptures and kitchen countertops. In '대리석 무늬' it describes a pattern even when the material is not real stone. A similar stone is '화강암' (granite).

examples.en: My bladder is weak, so I go to the bathroom often.

examples.ko: 방광 건강을 위해 물을 충분히 마시세요.
examples.en: Drink enough water for the sake of your bladder health.
I had a bladder test at the hospital.

examples.ko: 방광염 때문에 소변을 볼 때 아팠어요.
examples.en: It hurt when I urinated because of a bladder infection.
I heard stones can form in the bladder.
Please empty your bladder and then enter the exam room.

explain: 소변을 모아 두는 몸속 기관이에요. 병원에서는 '방광염'이라는 말로 자주 만나요. '방광이 터질 것 같다'는 소변이 아주 급하다는 과장된 농담으로도 써요.
explain_en: It is the organ in the body that stores urine. At hospitals you often meet it in the word '방광염' (cystitis). '방광이 터질 것 같다' is also used as an exaggerated joke meaning you urgently need the toilet.

examples.en: The teacher handed out the test papers to the students.

examples.ko: 회의 전에 자료를 미리 배부해 주세요.
examples.en: Please hand out the materials before the meeting.
The district office hands out trash bags for free.
They are handing out notices at the event hall.
They lined people up to hand out masks.
They didn't hand out the materials, so I didn't know the content.

explain: 여러 사람에게 서류나 물건을 나눠 줄 때 쓰는 격식 있는 말이에요. 일상 대화에서는 '나눠 주다'가 더 자연스러워요. 학교, 회사, 관공서 안내문에서 자주 보여요.
explain_en: It is a formal word for giving out documents or items to many people. In everyday talk, '나눠 주다' sounds more natural. You often see it in notices from schools, companies and government offices.

examples.en: Our family divides the housework by day of the week.
We decided to split the shipping fee half and half.
How should we divide up the presentation prep?
If we share the cost, the burden gets smaller.

examples.ko: 일을 공평하게 분담하지 않아서 불만이 생겼어요.
examples.en: The work wasn't divided fairly, so complaints came up.
The friends shared the travel expenses equally.

explain: 일이나 비용을 여러 사람이 나눠서 각자 맡을 때 써요. 그냥 '나누다'보다 각자 책임을 진다는 느낌이 있어요. 일상에서는 '반반 내다'처럼도 말하고, '역할 분담', '비용 분담'이 자주 쓰는 짝이에요.
explain_en: It is used when several people divide work or costs and each takes a part. Compared with plain '나누다', it carries a sense that each person is responsible for a share. In daily talk people also say things like '반반 내다', and '역할 분담' and '비용 분담' are common pairings.

examples.ko: 은행 직원 사칭 전화가 늘고 있어요.
examples.en: Calls impersonating bank employees are increasing.
I reported an account impersonating a celebrity.

examples.ko: 사칭은 큰 문제가 될 수 있어요.
examples.en: Impersonation can become a serious problem.

examples.ko: 경찰 사칭 문자에 속지 않도록 조심하세요.
examples.en: Be careful not to be fooled by texts impersonating the police.
Many people have suffered from impersonation scams.
If you suspect impersonation, check right away.

explain: 남의 이름, 직업, 기관을 거짓으로 내세워 속이는 일을 말해요. 보이스피싱 문자나 SNS 가짜 계정 이야기에서 '사칭 계정', '사칭 전화'로 자주 나와요. 단순히 흉내 내는 '따라 하다'와 달리 속이려는 목적이 있어요.
explain_en: It means falsely claiming someone else's name, job or organization in order to deceive. It often appears as '사칭 계정' and '사칭 전화' in talk about phishing texts and fake social media accounts. Unlike simple imitation, '따라 하다', it has the purpose of deceiving.

examples.ko: 누가 우리 회사 직원을 사칭해서 전화했어요.
examples.en: Someone called, pretending to be an employee of our company.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 의사를 사칭하고 돈을 받았어요.
examples.en: That person posed as a doctor and took money.
There are many accounts impersonating a famous singer.
I received a text pretending to be from a delivery company.
You must not pose as a police officer.
A person who tried to pose as a big-company employee was caught.

explain: 'N을/를 사칭하다'로 쓰고, 남의 신분이나 기관 이름을 거짓으로 내세워 속일 때 써요. 장난으로 흉내 내는 건 '따라 하다', '흉내 내다'를 쓰고, 사칭하다는 사기나 범죄 이야기에 어울려요. 주로 '사칭한 문자', '사칭하는 계정'처럼 꾸며 주는 말로 나와요.
explain_en: It is used as 'N을/를 사칭하다' when falsely claiming someone's identity or an organization's name to deceive. For playful imitation, use '따라 하다' or '흉내 내다'; 사칭하다 fits fraud and crime stories. It often appears as a modifier, as in '사칭한 문자' and '사칭하는 계정'.
